title: qa
universal_lens: The CI-equivalent gate defines a composite indicator function over a discrete sequence of software integrity constraints. The system state transitions through a Markovian chain of verification operators, where the global pass condition is the logical conjunction of all local type-checking, linting, and evaluation predicates.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps each local gate execution to a Bayesian hypothesis test regarding codebase health. A passing gate updates the posterior probability of deployment readiness, while a failing gate triggers a conformal prediction interval collapse, isolating the exact verbatim failure line as the primary anomaly signal.
gse_mapping: In GSE, the pipeline represents a strict state-transition automaton. The 'report-only' constraint enforces an observation operator that measures the current configuration without applying a unitary transformation (fix), preserving the pre-measurement state for subsequent explicit user-driven interventions.

primitives.name: Sequential Gate Evaluator
primitives.verbatim_quote: Produce one table row per gate: gate name, pass/fail, and the first failing line of output (verbatim) when it fails.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: I_{\text{gate}}: dimensionless boolean indicator; s_t: discrete system state at time t; \mathcal{O}_k: observable metric for gate k (dimensionless score); \theta_k: acceptance threshold (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Gates are evaluated sequentially or in parallel with independent failure modes; outputs are deterministic given state s_t.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs if N \to \infty causing combinatorial explosion of failure states, or if \mathcal{O}_k becomes non-deterministic due to environmental stochasticity.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE defensive coverage checks, where individual player positioning gates must collectively satisfy a spatial integrity predicate before a play is deemed valid.
layer2.telemetry: Gate pass rate and mean time to first failure line extraction.

primitives.name: Observational Freeze Constraint
primitives.verbatim_quote: Fix nothing — this command reports only, unless the user explicitly asks for fixes afterward.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \nabla_{\text{fix}}: gradient operator over fix-actions; \mathcal{L}: loss function of the codebase; s_t: system state; t: discrete time step.
primitives.assumptions: The system possesses the capability to compute gradients/fixes but actively zeroes them out until an external trigger.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if the observational process itself induces side-effects (e.g., mutable global state during testing), violating the zero-gradient assumption.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's passive telemetry collection phase, where sensor data is ingested and scored without triggering automated coaching interventions until a human analyst requests action.
layer2.telemetry: Zero mutation count during the reporting phase.

primitives.name: Environmental Coverage Gap

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Delta_{\text{coverage}}: set difference of job definitions; \mathcal{J}_{\text{remote}}: set of remote CI jobs; \mathcal{J}_{\text{local}}: set of locally executed jobs.
primitives.assumptions: Local environment lacks certain infrastructure dependencies (e.g., Prisma test-DB, production Next.js build servers) required by \mathcal{J}_{\text{remote}}.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if \Delta_{\text{coverage}} contains critical security or integration jobs, rendering the local pass insufficient for deployment guarantees.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's distinction between practice drill metrics and full-game situational stress tests; local runs lack the adversarial pressure of the full production environment.
layer2.telemetry: Cardinality of \Delta_{\text{coverage}} and risk-weighted severity of missing jobs.

This operates as a high-dimensional boolean filter, where the system state $s_t$ must reside within the intersection of all valid hyperplanes defined by thresholds $\theta_k$. The extraction of the 'first failing line' acts as a precise localization operator, identifying the minimal perturbation vector responsible for violating the constraint.

Second, the Observational Freeze Constraint introduces a temporal boundary condition on the optimization landscape. By enforcing $\nabla_{\text{fix}} \mathcal{L} = \mathbf{0}$, the system decouples the measurement phase from the actuation phase. This prevents premature convergence or unintended state mutations during the diagnostic sweep, ensuring that the reported anomalies reflect the true underlying state rather than artifacts of the repair mechanism.

Third, the Environmental Coverage Gap highlights the duality between local approximations and global truth. The set difference $\Delta_{\text{coverage}}$ quantifies the epistemic uncertainty introduced by running a subset of the full CI matrix. In a Bayesian sense, a clean local run provides a likelihood update, but the posterior probability of total system health remains bounded by the missing remote jobs (e.g., secret-scan, dependency-audit). The interplay of these primitives creates a robust, multi-layered verification protocol that balances computational efficiency (local fast runs) with comprehensive assurance (remote CI mirroring), directly mapping to complex decision-making architectures in sports intelligence where rapid diagnostics must coexist with deep, context-aware validation.
